questions.q: Per this lesson, why isn't a successful communication plan (Lesson 18) enough to produce adoption by itself?
options: Awareness that a process matters is different from knowing how to actually do it — training closes that specific gap
Communication plans are inherently unreliable
Training is required by regulation regardless of communication
Awareness and ability are the same thing, so this isn't actually true
questions.explain: The lesson draws a direct line between awareness (communication's job) and ability (training's job) as two separate problems.

questions.q: How does the lesson distinguish process training from data literacy?
options: Process training is narrow and tied to one specific tool or workflow; data literacy is broader, more durable understanding that makes future process training land faster
They are two names for the exact same activity
Data literacy is only for executives, and process training is only for analysts
Process training never goes stale, while data literacy expires every quarter
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates narrow, tool-specific process training from broader, durable data literacy.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a single one-hour training session delivered once is a weak approach?
options: Attendees forget most of it within weeks, and anyone hired afterward never gets it at all
One-hour sessions are against company policy
It's too expensive compared to other options
It always produces immediate expert-level ability
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out forgetting over time and new hires missing it entirely as reasons a single session underperforms.

questions.q: What does 'reinforcement at point of use' mean in this lesson?
options: Help embedded directly in the tool or moment someone needs it, like a tooltip or help link, instead of a training session held once
Repeating the same one-hour training session every month
Sending a reminder email with no actual instructional content
Requiring a certification exam before tool access is granted
questions.explain: The lesson defines this as help placed right where and when someone needs it, not buried in a training portal.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say data literacy investment is often easier to justify to a skeptical stakeholder than process-specific training?
options: It's a durable organizational capability useful even outside the formal governance process, not just compliance overhead
It costs nothing to deliver
It's legally required in every jurisdiction
Process-specific training provides no value at all
questions.explain: The lesson frames data literacy as broadly useful beyond governance compliance, which makes its value easier to argue for.
